item.title: We’ve been busy building and releasing but it’s high time to share some major news: @sovtechfund is investing nearly €500K into #chatmail This 18-month commitment supports chatmail maintainers keeping the core infrastructure secure and evolving, on top of which several apps are built (but not STF funded): #DeltaChat @arcanechat @deltatouch Parla on Gnome A huge thank you to the Sovereign Tech Fund for investing in open, secure and decentralized communication! https://www.sovereign.tech/tech/chatmail

"it's always the receiver that determines the meaning of a message" is a famous opening quote at the first symposium on self organizing systems in Chicago, 1959. This and many other findings from those circles re-appear in our day to day discussions. We are doing next steps towards automating planet-wide decentralized onboarding, including in Internet islands, without resorting to a central list of relays. Good news: we have now officially lost track of even the number of existing relays 😂

Making sure that deleted messages are actually deleted and unrecoverable is more involved than most folks think. The FBI could recently recover deleted Signal messages from an iOS phone because the notifications you see on your phone were stored in an extra database. Apple has now fixed this, also making #deltachat iOS users safer. Few know that so called "forward secrecy" is all about deleted messages becoming unrecoverable, see https://autocrypt2.org for our plans https://www.heise.de/en/news/FBI-extraction-of-deleted-Signal-messages-Apple-secures-iPhones-better-11269038.html

#deltachat user profiles are private and invisible to the public. No one can discover you, or your children, via phone numbers or any other public handle. Chat profiles exist only on user devices. No PIN and no "SMS verification code" ever asked or needed. The lack of "public discovery" also means you don't auto-discover others via phone numbers or other public handles. Getting in contact with others is "opt in": you scan a QR code or click an invite link to join a group or open a chat.

This morning nine.testrun.org was briefly unavailable, some network problem. A good time to remind everyone to add a second relay to your #deltachat app: 1. Go to https://chatmail.at/relays randomly choose one of the listed relay pages and copy the invitation code to your clipboard 2. In delta chat settings go to advanced/relays and tap "add relay" and paste the invitation code 3. That's it. If one relay is unavailable you still can receive and send messages. https://delta.chat/en/2026-03-31-zero#maximizing-availability-and-resilience-through-multi-path-delivery

"Popularity is overrated" is an often occuring phrase in our circles. Which is of course nonsense because only what is popular, counts, right? Only what everybody else does is a valid choice, right? #deltachat #chatmail and #webxdc are used in private places and communities that people are molding for themselves. We are just providing tools and approaches that work ... At least most of the time 😅 "Nothing works all the time" is another project mantra. Brb preparing the next releases :) Photo of a beautiful park in the black forest where a few of us are gathering to discuss the various authoritarian tendencies in platforms, countries, infrastructures and minds ... And plotting our next steps on a beautiful sunny day with lots of green grass, violet flowery trees and shadows in the sun

Apart from the new #Gnome effort, there also is an interesting experiment of a #Rust terminal-client with #Ratatui -- for others to start from should they feel they need some enjoyable distraction :) https://git.sakamoto.pl/j-g00da/deltarat-experiments #Chatmail clients typically use the Rust core library which provides all networking, cryptography, persistence, real-time networking, mail relay/server interop. Documentation to help with writing clients is scattered, but at least there are plenty examples to learn from.

the public #chatmail relay list https://chatmail.at/relays covers about ~20% or so of chat relays we heart about and have traces or hints from, and we definitely don't see everything -- which is how it should be :) Best of all: you can now start using multiple relays for your chat profiles, so even if one relay goes down or is blocked temporarily, chatting continues. https://delta.chat/en/2026-03-31-zero#maximizing-availability-and-resilience-through-multi-path-delivery

What if all public funding and all private donations to our efforts stop tomorrow? Users should be fine for years thanks to the wonderful world-wide community of #chatmail relay operators 💜 Relays are dirt cheap to run. Also, our developments are much cheaper and less complex compared to what we know from comparable efforts. No worries though! We currently have moneys to help sustain ~15 contributors, with a sum similar to what other projects pay for their foundation president/CEO alone :)

RE: https://chaos.social/@delta/115866917974514933 Do you want to live in a world where private digital communication is not possible anymore? That's a growing reality for many people world-wide. Private communication is extremely important to salvage into the digital realm and it's not just about encryption, but about the ability to choose your own identities privately, without state sanctioning. It needs caring for solving real problems, in real implementations, for real people, and not just some riding on grand ideas. Just saying :)

#deltachat contributors range from age 16 to 65, spanning diverse genders and even more countries and cultures. We have many discussions, and also conflicts but we usually don't carry those out in big public groups but rather go for 1:1s and generally small-group discussions. There is no central assembly or board that decides everything. It's more chaotic and admittedly hard to get an overview on, but thats' also how the yearly #CCC congress comes about, which many of us regularly attend.

Under the hood, we are using IETF Internet Messaging specifications commonly tagged as "email". Sounds old, right? Actually there is a lot of new stuff going on! For example, #chatmail apps now fully support: - RFC9788 ("Header Protection") to achieve minimal metadata - RFC9580 ("OpenPGP") to use modern cryptography By comparison, "Messaging Layer Security (MLS)" has an older numbered RFC9420 (and doesn't have mass-usable app releases). Maybe time to revisit old/new assumptions? :)

After three intense months of work from more than a dozen contributors, #deltachat 2.48 releases are rolling. Maybe the most feature-packed releases ever? - "zero metadata" messaging - native Audio/Video calls on Android and iOS, as well as UbuntuTouch - Group and Channel descriptions - A new background audio player - Revamped Download-on-Demand and, last but not least, the long-awaited next-generation of messaging resiliency through "multi-path" routing .... https://delta.chat/en/2026-03-31-zero

RE: https://pouet.chapril.org/@agenda_du_libre/116293754039872689 swiss news: a new chatmail relay https://chatsecure.ch ... hosted in denmark, however :) also there is an upocoming event in Môtiers in two days. And there was a podcast featuring delta chat last year: https://gnulinux.ch/ciw152-podcast

End-to-End Encryption is good but metadata protection counts as much. Names, group descriptions and memberships, avatars, who talks to whom ... Both #deltachat and #signal go to great length to protect all the metadata that WhatsApp grants itself gratuitously. #Matrix stores similar scales of metadata on their servers, even if you can choose which server stores it. Everything is better than #Telegram which additionally stores message contents in all group chats/channels and most 1:1 chats. screenshot of artifical WhatsApp screen courtesy of @fex@cfn.social [Lock Icon] Your personal messages are end-to-end encrypted¹ But: When you message someone is saved forever. When you type is saved forever. Your approximate location is saved forever. Every profile picture is saved forever. Every status update is saved forever. Every group name is saved forever. Every group description is saved forever. Every community name is saved forever. Every community description is saved forever. Every time you join a group is saved forever. Every time you leave a group is saved forever. Every new contact is saved forever. Deleting a contact is saved forever. What you search for is saved forever. Who you call and when is saved forever. When you hang up is saved forever. When you’re online is saved forever. When you’re offline is saved forever. Every link you open is stored forever. Your phone model is stored forever. Your operating system is stored forever. Your battery level is stored forever. Your signal strength is stored forever. Your app version is stored forever. Your mobile network is stored forever. Your Wi-Fi network is stored forever. ..... Your IP addresses are stored forever. Your meta ID is stored forever. Your settings are stored forever. ¹Just in case your contacts don’t back up your messages with Google or Apple

The last two weeks saw a dev gathering in the black forest from several in #chatmail, #deltachat and #webxdc communiities, also joined by @n0iroh and @rpgp folks. The tech demos and hacking results we presented to each other, were pretty mind blowing and tracing a path to very interesting futures, delivered in working code, not just some grand plan. Let us just say for now that we are getting to the fun parts of an age old http://testrun.org motto :) happy #equinox! May the tides turn! Top part of the https://testrun.org web page with the motto "experimenting with the future of email". Below is a dinosaur head with an open mouth about to swallow a zeppelin

Fun funding fact: If we had 10 times more money to develop #deltachat , the #chatmail relay network and the #webxdc secure mini app ecosystem, we would still have ten times less than what signal has (let alone Whatsapp or telegram). But we don't want to increase nudging people for donations, as we have many users who don't even have a legal way to send us money, let alone the means. It is a special kind of reward that delta works where most if not all other messengers fail to work for users.

OH in some chaos circles "#deltachat is the new emacs of operating systems" ... We are not sure about that 😂 but what we do know is we are soon bringing out releases that we have been working towards for 12 months in multiple already released steps. The funniest thing? Nothing changes on the surface which was precisely what we worked for so long ... more soon, after internal testing and some pending bug fixes land :) and no worries, there will also be interesting visible changes. Stay tuned :)

Our strong focus on end to end encryption and zero metadata does mean that one of the original project notions of "you can use delta chat as a lightweight cleartext email client and your contacts don't need to care" was deprioritized since some time now and remains available rather for specialists only. It used to be encrypted mail that was hard to do and only for experts. Delta kind of reversed this. Now it's hard to do cleartext. But you can self host your mailbox addresses. No changes there!

some insights from #deltachat forum gardening 🌸 - we’re getting about 7 new feature proposals per week, with over 1k ideas shared so far - we aim to keep things simple and focused, so we often have to say "no!", but: - we do listen: over the years, we’ve fulfilled about ONE THIRD of your wishes 🧞‍♂️ your pushes are appreciated ❤️ https://support.delta.chat/c/features/6
